findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on fallible I/O result
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable shard file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed error variant

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - console I/O inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Hidden I/O in what should be a pure/parsing path pollutes stdout, makes the function side-effectful, breaks composability and testability, and violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell
findings.fix: Remove println entirely. If instrumentation is needed, pass a callback or return metadata separately from the shell layer

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - unwrap on parse AND lossy as cast
findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric field panics via unwrap; even if parse succeeds, any u32 > 65535 silently truncates to u16 via lossy cast, corrupting domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::from_str with map_err for typed parse error; remove the as u16 cast entirely by parsing directly to u16

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] - unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via index-out-of-bounds at runtime; empty lines or trailing newlines trigger this
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (_name, value_str) and parse value_str fallibly

findings.problem: load_shards fuses file I/O, string allocation, parsing, console I/O, and domain construction into a single function
findings.failure_mode: No separation of concerns; cannot test parsing logic without a real file, cannot reuse parsing without triggering disk reads and stdout writes, violates Parse-Dont-Validate and Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> function. Keep load_shards as the shell that handles I/O and calls the pure parser

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 primitives; no parse boundary or smart constructor enforces domain rules
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with any string (empty, whitespace, invalid Unicode) and any u16 value, including values that are semantically invalid for the domain; invalid states are representable
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide a parse constructor fn try_record(name: &str, value_str: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>, and add domain invariants (non-empty name, value in valid range)

findings.problem: line.split(',').collect() into Vec<String> allocates intermediate collection of all parts instead of parsing one key-value pair
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every line, splits on ALL commas (a name containing a comma produces extra parts), and the collect-into-Vec pattern is explicitly forbidden in the hardening checklist as an allocation/shape mistake
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to split on the first comma only, then parse the right side; discard the left field with let (_name, value_str)

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_shards file I/O and parsing path
findings.failure_mode: No measured baseline for throughput/latency; cannot prove performance of this hot path or detect regressions from future changes
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring load_shards against representative shard files with multiple line counts

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_shards I/O and parsing throughput
no profiler evidence for allocation hot spots in the parse loop
no allocation audit for Vec<String> per-line intermediate allocations
no command-truth evidence (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test) was run or recorded
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands executed. The crate contains 6 BLOCKER violations including unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, hidden console I/O, and absent parse boundary. All must be repaired before the code can be considered Holzman-compliant.
